audit.whatIsWrong: content win[1] reads Yasuo while whys[1] says 'Still yours at 2'. win[2] and win[3] read Skill while whys[2] and whys[3] say Level 3 gives Aatrox the full rotation to walk him down and 4-5 the sweetspot combo dominates the extended brawl. win[5] reads Yasuo while whys[5] says first-item drain makes extended trades one-sided for Aatrox.
audit.why: Yasuo's only defensive cooldown against Aatrox's combo is Wind Wall on 25s at rank 1, and it does not stop The Darkin Blade. The packet chart reads Aatrox for six stages and Yasuo only at Two+ items. 52.64% over 4535 games.
audit.corrected: Levels 1 through First item all read Aatrox; Two+ items stays Yasuo.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] still says 'commit only when his Windwall is down' — misspelled, and attached to the wrong ability, since the Level 6 spike is about ultimates. Last Breath is never named and never given a cooldown.
audit.why: Last Breath is 70/50/30 and it can only be cast on an enemy who is already Airborne. Against Aatrox that means it is gated on someone else's knockup, not his own — a Yasuo alone in a side lane cannot open with it. Wind Wall is 25/23/21/19/17.
audit.corrected: Last Breath named with its 70s cooldown and its airborne requirement in spikes[1]; 'Windwall' corrected to Wind Wall in whys[1] and whys[4].

audit.why: The Wind Wall interaction has already been fixed in this file since my first pass: spikes[0], early and mid now correctly state that the wall eats Infernal Chains but not The Darkin Blade, which is the decisive fact. Nothing further needed there. The remaining gap is Way of the Wanderer — the entry calls it 'his shield' and 'Flow shield' without naming it, and never says it only triggers on damage from a champion or monster.
audit.corrected: Way of the Wanderer named in spikes[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Sweeping Blade is described as 'E dashes through minions' with no mention of its restriction.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Cannot be re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds.' His escape therefore depends on having several separate bodies to hop between. Pulling the fight off the wave, or engaging right after he has dashed through the minion beside him, strands him with no reset — which is what converts the 25s Wind Wall window into a kill instead of a chase.
audit.corrected: Stated in late: fight off the wave so Sweeping Blade has no fresh target to re-cast on.

edits.before: World Ender's combat stats and heal amp let you brute-force through his shield and drain back the poke; commit only when his Windwall is down.
edits.after: World Ender's stats and heal amp brute-force Way of the Wanderer's shield; Last Breath (70s) needs an airborne target, so he waits on an ally.

edits.before: After first item your drain and sweetspot pattern keep the 1v1 favoured, but once Yasuo completes two crit items with R available off ally knockups, his burst and teamfight ceiling climb past yours and the matchup tips to him. Play the sidelane, itemize a bit of armor, and force him to duel you where sustain decides it rather than grouping into his AoE.
edits.after: After first item your drain and sweetspot pattern keep the 1v1 favoured, but two crit items plus Last Breath off ally knockups push his ceiling past yours. Play the sidelane and fight off the wave: Sweeping Blade cannot re-cast on the same enemy for a few seconds, so with no fresh minion beside him he cannot reset spacing at all. Make him duel you where sustain decides it.

edits.before: Still yours at 2; his Windwall and shield only blunt trades you can restart with drain.
edits.after: Still yours at 2; Wind Wall and his shield only blunt trades you restart with drain.

edits.before: World Ender's stats and heal amp overpower his shield when Windwall is down.
edits.after: World Ender's stats and heal amp overpower his shield once Wind Wall is spent.

edits.before: Yasuo changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Yasuo wave dashes, Wind Wall, third Q swing (the knock-up), and R. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Yasuo wants to enter inside Aatrox clean Q hits on the outer edge (where it hurts most), force melee trades, and punish Aatrox after Q/E are down.
edits.after: Yasuo changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Wind Wall (W, 25s), which eats Infernal Chains but never touches The Darkin Blade, and Sweeping Blade hopping between minions to reset spacing. Aatrox wins by leading with the Q pattern straight through the wall, holding the chain until the wall is spent, and dragging the fight off the wave — Sweeping Blade cannot re-cast on the same enemy, so with no fresh body he is stranded in the trade.
